extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians/computer-algebra programmers) working with multigradings and modules; users of the multigrading.lib library
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR's multigrading.lib: how to call routines that compute/check multidegrees, multigraded Groebner bases, syzygies, resolutions, tensor products, Hilbert series, and related linear-algebra normal forms. Each entry gives usage, purpose, notes, returns and examples for applying the routine correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: equalMultiDeg
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests if the exponent vectors of two monomials (given by exp1 and exp2) represent the same multidegree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: equalMultiDeg(exp1, exp2[, V]); intvec exp1, exp2, intmat V. Note: the integer matrix V encodes multidegrees of module components, if module component is present in exp1 and exp2. Example shown comparing leadexponents of polynomials under a base multigrading; returns 1 for equal multidegree, 0 otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegGroebner
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the multigraded standard/Groebner basis of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegGroebner(I); I is a poly/vector/ideal/module. Note: I must be multigraded homogeneous. Returns an ideal/module containing the computed basis. Example demonstrates computing multigraded GB of a module, printing module multigrading, multidegrees, checking isHomogeneous, and then computing syzygies and calling multiDegGroebner on the syzygy module.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegSyzygy
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the multigraded syzygy module of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegSyzygy(I); I is an ideal or a module. Purpose: computes the multigraded syzygy module of I. Returns: module, the syzygy module of I. Note: generators of I must be multigraded homogeneous. Example shows creating module M with setBaseMultigrading and setModuleGrading, checking isHomogeneous(M) == 1, then computing S = multiDegSyzygy(M) and printing module grading and multidegrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegModulo
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the multigraded 'modulo' module of I and J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegModulo(I); I, J are ideals or modules. Purpose: computes the multigraded 'modulo' module of I and J. Returns: module (see 'modulo' command). Note: I and J should have the same multigrading, and their generators must be multigraded homogeneous. Example: computing modulo(h1, h2) with given base multigrading; prints members, module units multigrading, multidegrees and isHomogeneous(K)==1.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegResolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the multigraded resolution of I of specified length (or whole resolution) and optionally returns the minimal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegResolution(I,l,[f]); I is poly/vector/ideal/module; l,f are integers. Purpose: computes the multigraded resolution of I of length l, or whole resolution if l is zero. Returns minimal resolution if optional argument 1 is supplied. Note: input must have multigraded-homogeneous generators. The returned list is truncated beginning with the first zero differential. Example shows computing syzygies, Groebnerizing, then list L = multiDegResolution(m, 0, 1) and iterating over L printing module multigrading and multiDeg(L[j]).

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegTensor
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the multigraded tensor product of two multigraded modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegTensor(m, n), m,n modules or matrices. Purpose: Computes the multigraded tensor product of two multigraded modules. Return: a module. Example: shows setting base multigrading, constructing modules mm and nn with setModuleGrading, calling mmtnn = multiDegTensor(mm, nn), printing the result and getModuleGrading(mmtnn). Also shows comparison with tensorMod(mm,nn) from homolog.lib and verifies equality (prints a-b = all zeros).

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegTor
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure heading present for multiDegTor (multigraded Tor computation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D.15.23.44 multiDegTor is listed as a procedure name in the library index/contents; chunk shows the heading only. Presumably computes multigraded Tor groups for modules/ideals. (No detailed usage/purpose/notes were present in this chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: defineHomogeneous
rubrics_metrics.description: Yields a matrix which has to be appended to the grading group matrix to make the polynomial f homogeneous in the grading by grad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: defineHomogeneous(f[, G]); polynomial f, integer matrix G. Purpose: produce a matrix M to append to grading group matrix so that f becomes homogeneous. Example: with base multigrading grad and f = x2y3 - z5 + x - 3zx, defineHomogeneous(f) returns a matrix M; defineHomogeneous(f, grad) == M returns 1; isHomogeneous(f) before is 0, after setBaseMultigrading(grad, M) isHomogeneous(f) == 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: pushForward
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the finest grading of the image ring which makes the map f a map of graded rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: pushForward(f); Purpose: computes the finest grading of the image ring making map f graded. Note: The group map between the two grading groups is given by transpose((Id, 0)). Be aware the group spanned by columns of the grading group matrix may not be a subgroup of the grading group; still all columns are needed to find the correct image of the preimage gradings. Example demonstrates pushing forward a map f between rings and then calling getVariableWeights() and getLattice() to see new grading on the image ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: gradiator
rubrics_metrics.description: Coarsens the grading of the basering until the polynomial or ideal h becomes homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: coarsens the grading of the base ring until the polynomial or ideal h becomes homogeneous. Example: after setBaseMultigrading(g,l) and defining an ideal i with non-homogeneous generators, calling gradiator(i) returns 1 and getLattice() shows updated lattice; isHomogeneous(i) becomes 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: hermiteNormalForm
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the (lower triangular) Hermite Normal Form of the matrix A by column operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: hermiteNormalForm(A); Purpose: computes the Hermite Normal Form. Return: intmat, the Hermite Normal Form of A. Example: several intmat examples printed to illustrate output; the procedure is used to obtain column-operation normal form helpful for lattice/gradings manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: smithNormalForm
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the Smith Normal Form of an integer matrix A (and optionally the transforming matrices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: smithNormalForm(A[,opt]); intmat A. Purpose: Computes the Smith Normal Form of A. Return: if no optional argument given: intmat D (the Smith Normal Form); otherwise returns list [P, D, Q] with P*A*Q == D. Example shows calling smithNormalForm(A) and smithNormalForm(A,5) to obtain P,D,Q and verifies l[1]*A*l[3] equals diagonal D, and det(l[1])==det(l[3])==1.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbertSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the multigraded Hilbert Series of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: hilbertSeries(I); I is poly/vector/ideal/module. Purpose: computes the multigraded Hilbert Series of I. Notes: input must have multigraded-homogeneous generators; Multigrading should be positive. Returns a ring in variables t_(i), s_(i) with polynomials numerator1/2 and denominator1/2 whose quotients give the series; s_(i) variables are inverses of t_(i). Examples show usage on modules and ideals, printing numerator1/2 and denominator1/2, factorizing, and interpreting series; many example cases with various base multigradings and ideals are provided and the output and checks (isHomogeneous, multiDeg, etc.) are shown.
